description: Records up to ten polyphonic tracks of control voltage as a standard MIDI file, one row of jacks per track

inputs.text: Sets the tempo written into the MIDI file, 120 BPM doubling for every volt, the same scaling Impromptu's Clocked uses; the reading is shown on the red display
Starts recording while the voltage is above 0V and stops when it falls back; with a cable here the REC button is ignored
The note pitch for that track, 1V per octave, one note per polyphonic channel; 0V is middle C and the pitch is rounded to the nearest semitone
The note gates for that track, one per polyphonic channel, a note sounding while the channel is at 1V or above
The note velocities for that track, one per polyphonic channel, 0-10V by default and rescaled by the VEL Input Range menu; unpatched, every note is recorded at velocity 100
The aftertouch for that track, 0-10V by default and rescaled by the AFT Input Range menu; only the first channel is read, and that one value is written to every note of the track
The pitchbend for that track, -5V to 5V by default and rescaled by the PW Input Range menu; one channel only, and it is always written as a 14-bit value
The modulation wheel for that track, 0-10V by default and rescaled by the MW Input Range menu; one channel only, sent as control change 1, or as 1 and 33 with MW is 14bit turned on

outputs.text: Goes to 10V while events are actually being captured, which is after the first note when Start at first note gate is on, and as soon as recording starts when it is off

notes: nothing is written until a target file is chosen; pick one from Output File on the menu, or a file dialog opens the first time you record
the REC button starts and stops the recording and turns red while it is running; it is not a parameter, so no click on it reaches this help
a cable in the REC jack takes the button out of use altogether
a track is recorded only when at least one jack in its row has a cable in it
with a cable in a row's gate jack and none in its pitch jack, each polyphonic channel gets a note of its own, from middle C upwards by a semitone, which suits drum gates
the MIDI file is written when recording stops, so stop the recorder before looking for the file
the lamp under the ACTIVE jack is lit whenever that output is high
a MIDIRecorderCC placed immediately to the right adds control change columns to the same ten tracks, and several can be chained one after another
menu: Output File — chooses the MIDI file to write; the path is shown in place of Select... once one has been chosen
Append -001, -002, etc. — writes a new numbered file each time rather than overwriting the one already there
Start at first note gate — holds the recording back until the first note gate arrives, so events line up with a bar; earlier pitchbend, modulation and aftertouch are dropped
VEL Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the velocity jacks, from -10 to 10 down to 0 to 1
AFT Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the aftertouch jacks
PW Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the pitchbend jacks
MW Input Range — sets the voltage span read from the modulation jacks
MW is 14bit — writes the modulation value as control change 1 and 33 together, at 14-bit resolution, instead of control change 1 alone
